messages:
anya: Quick idea from today's sync: attach per-layer confidence tags to quant profiles and let the runtime use prompt-aware hints to relax precision only on low-confidence layers.

tomas: interesting. so rather than a single profile-level floor, we get layer-level signals?

anya: exactly. a profile would carry a small vector like [0.98,0.95,0.90,...] representing acceptable quality per transformer block. runtime compares per-layer degradations (from sampled shadow runs) and chooses bitpath accordingly.

reza: how do we compute per-layer degradation cheaply in prod? we can't run full shadow per request.

anya: two parts: 1) offline calibration that builds a per-layer sensitivity map per model & quant scheme, 2) lightweight online signals (logit-delta estimates from kv-cache / last-token surprisal proxies) to decide which layers are "sensitive" for this prompt.

kai: so prompt-aware hints -> runtime can skip lowering precision on sensitive layers for a given request. That could preserve quality while saving cost. Nice.

anya: sample API sketch:```json
POST /v1/generate
{
 "model":"redwood-7b-qpt",
 "precision_profile":"per-layer-econ-v2",
 "prompt_hints":{ "important_spans": [[12,45]], "sensitivity": "low" },
 "max_tokens": 128
}
```

reza: prompt_hints might be user-provided or auto-extracted by a preprocessor. must be optional and sanitized.

anya: yes. default is no hints -> runtime uses conservative stack. we should encourage SDKs to provide simple helpers (e.g., highlight_completion_context()).

kai: ops concerns: complexity for caching and batching. different bitpaths per-layer will complicate kernel selection and batching.

tomas: true. we should constrain runtime choices: only allow up to N distinct layer-precision classes per model in a single batch. and fall back to model-level precision if batching can't satisfy heterogeneity.

ops-bot: note: please run performance benchmark if allowing per-layer heterogeneity in a routing batch.

reza: storage: profiles must include the sensitivity map and a small manifest of allowed per-layer bitwidths. example profile snippet:
```json
{
 "name":"per-layer-econ-v2",
 "allowed_layer_bits": [8,4],
 "layer_confidence_thresholds": [0.98,0.95,0.9,...],
 "preproc_hint_policy":"auto-suggest"
}
```

anya: evaluation plan: attach a per-profile eval bundle with prompts that exercise headwise and layerwise failure modes. run shadow sampling at small scale to validate before enabling.

kai: runtime implementation note: we can compress per-layer vectors (quantize to int8) and cache in memory per model artifact. selection logic must be O(L) and fast.

tomas: rollback / safety: keep a global kill-switch and per-profile hard-failback to model-level precision. also add a degradation-score that aggregates layer deltas into single metric for alerting.

reza: customer override: allow org-level policy to disable per-layer optimization (some customers want consistent determinism). precedence: request hint > endpoint > org > global.

anya: UX: Console should show heatmap for layer sensitivity and estimated cost delta if per-layer optimization is enabled. include small simulation: "if enabled, expected tokens saved: 12%. expected BLEU/regression risk: 0.3%".

ops-bot: perf test queued: per-layer-batching-sim for redwood-7b-qpt scheduled. ETA 24h.

kai: next steps: I can prototype a kernel-selection shim that groups layers into classes for batching. reza can work the preproc hinter. anya will draft profile schema changes and eval plan. tomas will add safety gating to rollout playbook.

anya: sweet. I'll put a short RFC follow-up and a minimal PoC checklist. thanks all. :thumbsup:
